just_in.title: Viral Dhokla Chaat Is the Diwali Party Starter You Need
just_in.excerpt: Pooja Purohit's instant besan dhokla, steamed for 12-15 minutes and layered over yoghurt and chutneys with sev and pomegranate, gets a full chaat makeover for Diwali parties.
just_in.nri_angle: A vegetarian, no-fry Diwali party starter diaspora hosts can batch-make from Indian-grocer staples and assemble to order for guests.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Take besan in a large mixing bowl. Add salt and turmeric powder.
Gradually pour in water while whisking to make a lump-free batter. Add oil and lemon juice and mix well.
Just before steaming, add Eno to the batter and gently mix until it becomes light and fluffy.
Grease dhokla moulds with oil. Pour the batter into them, filling each mould only about three-fourths of the way. Place them in a steamer and cook for around 12-15 minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves and slit green chillies. Stir briefly and turn off the heat.
Remove the steamed dhokla from the moulds and place them on a plate. Pour the prepared tempering over them so that they absorb the flavours.
Take serving bowls and spread a layer of whisked yoghurt at the bottom. Add green chutney and tamarind chutney.
Place the steamed dhokla pieces over the yoghurt and chutneys. Sprinkle chaat masala and roasted cumin powder on top.
Garnish generously with sev, pomegranate pearls, boondi and freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Prepare the bowls just before serving so that the dhokla stays soft while the sev retains its crunch. Serve immediately.

food.title: Viral Dhokla Chaat Is the Diwali Party Starter You Need
food.excerpt: Pooja Purohit's instant besan dhokla, steamed for 12-15 minutes and layered over yoghurt and chutneys with sev and pomegranate, gets a full chaat makeover for Diwali parties.
food.nri_angle: A vegetarian, no-fry Diwali party starter diaspora hosts can batch-make from Indian-grocer staples and assemble to order for guests.
food.author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Take besan in a large mixing bowl. Add salt and turmeric powder.
Gradually pour in water while whisking to make a lump-free batter. Add oil and lemon juice and mix well.
Just before steaming, add Eno to the batter and gently mix until it becomes light and fluffy.
Grease dhokla moulds with oil. Pour the batter into them, filling each mould only about three-fourths of the way. Place them in a steamer and cook for around 12-15 minutes.
Heat oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves and slit green chillies. Stir briefly and turn off the heat.
Remove the steamed dhokla from the moulds and place them on a plate. Pour the prepared tempering over them so that they absorb the flavours.
Take serving bowls and spread a layer of whisked yoghurt at the bottom. Add green chutney and tamarind chutney.
Place the steamed dhokla pieces over the yoghurt and chutneys. Sprinkle chaat masala and roasted cumin powder on top.
Garnish generously with sev, pomegranate pearls, boondi and freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Prepare the bowls just before serving so that the dhokla stays soft while the sev retains its crunch. Serve immediately.

steps.detail: An invitation is not a nomination. Invited candidates apply to the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program for a provincial nomination.
If AAIP approves the application, it issues a nomination. The process can take several months, and Alberta had 495 of its 6,603 nomination spaces for 2026 still remaining as of November 4.

steps.step: Apply to the federal government for permanent residence
steps.detail: Nominees apply to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada for PR. Express Entry nominees receive 600 additional CRS points, which in practice guarantees a federal invitation.
